analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 4014-4695). The PR changes only documentation: ranges base 453 and 3219-3221, head 453-473, 3239-3242, 3255-3286. Those ranges fall outside the supplied BASE excerpts, so I could not examine the head lines. The patch excerpt is truncated and describes cluster-onboarding stop semantics (a stopsAsked counter in the cluster setup record, a ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked field, follower and leader end-on-stop behavior). The supplied text is documentation with no executable or security-control change.

The excerpts I examined describe existing behavior relevant to threat boundaries: cluster registration with equal TP shares only; the owner-authenticated link control channel and encrypted JACCL data plane; the fixed sanitized environment for owner child launch (no peer-supplied environment); the lane-count agreement checks; the prefix-cache tenant partitions (T-041); the msync(MS_INVALIDATE) cache drop, which needs no privileges and does not alter file bytes; and the Date comparison weak-import guard (A-018 availability). Nothing in these excerpts weakens any documented control, and I identified no invalidated threat assumption.

Remaining questions for integration: the new stop-count mechanism (stopsAsked) is peer-reported over the cluster control channel. Whether a peer or a replayed or stale reply can spoof or inhibit stops, or cause denial of service of onboarding, depends on the authentication of that channel and on the code, neither of which is in this batch. The patch is docs-only per the supplied metadata, so I report no finding. A reviewer with the code diff should confirm that it matches these docs and that the count comparison is made under the command lock.
